### power_ext_plan_change_rate (hub mid_term_plan_change_authorization_38205a51; computation plan_change_rate_computation_60e7beaf)
- Rule 1 (replaced_by: next billing cycle, new term from that date, plan-change rate "rather than the price-sheet offer", re-priced from the contract rate in force) and rule 2 (customer authorizes personally) → hub. Equivalent.
- **Prerequisite edge plan_change → rebill, form state.** `policy_source` "The plan-change rate is fixed only after the agreement's bill lines carry a rebill credit for every over-billed energy line whose correction is within the care agent's adjustment limit." → verbatim in mid_term_plan_change_authorization_38205a51 only; "fixed only after", state form. Resolution basis: offpeak_rebill_credit_posting "Once posted, the agreement's bill lines carry a rebill credit line pointing at the corrected line" (same words "rebill credit", "adjustment limit"); records: off-peak lines at 13.29 on a 0.00-multiplier plan; no rebill lines. Strength equal.
- **Prerequisite edge plan_change → signup, form state.** `policy_source` "A plan change is not recorded until the sign-up credit the current plan has earned stands on the agreement's bill lines." → verbatim in the same hub only; "not recorded until", state form. Resolution basis: signup_credit_posting_8f380fea "Once posted, the agreement's bill lines carry a sign-up credit line" and its earning rule; records: 7 completed cycles ≥ 3, no sign-up line. Strength equal (hard gate on recording).
- Neither depended-on policy's documents carries either sentence (verified).
- Baseline (contract rate in force, cents to 2 dp; price-sheet offer plays no part) and assembly (reductions summed, multiplier on the combined reduction, subtracted once, round at end) → computation doc. Equivalent; no default constants of its own.
- Factors: `billing_error_concession` → plan_change_billing_error_concession_26eb3190 (≥2 → 0.50, 1 → 0.25, 0 → none; rebill lines + open disputes; settled excluded); `plan_bundle_reduction` → plan_change_gas_bundle_reduction_1267a0ab (0.30/0.20/none; names Residential Natural Gas Supply); `plan_tenure_reduction` → plan_change_tenure_reduction_bb186f52 (≥24 → 0.30, 6–23 → 0.15, <6 → none); `plan_volume_reduction` → plan_change_volume_reduction_06645fa6 (≥1,200 → 0.20, 800–<1,200 → 0.10, <800 → none; all energy kWh ÷ cycles carrying an on-peak or all-hours line); `peak_cycle_reduction` → plan_change_peak_cycle_reduction_571e01d4 (≥900 → 0.15, 600–<900 → 0.08, <600 → none); `remaining_term_scaling` (method) → plan_change_remaining_term_scaling_9452d4fe (≥6 → ×1.5, 1–5 → ×1.2, <1 or no end date → as it stands). ## kb_to_source

- Every normative claim traced to a source atom. Derived restatements checked: "A customer who says the meter over-recorded their kWh is disputing the utility's reading …" (billing_correction_rules) ← base clause on meter readings; "Opening the dispute credits nothing on the bill" ← tool contract; "carried unrounded into the total" (fee returns) ← single final rounding in the source assembly; "A requested plan that passes Article 2 must still be one the premise and customer could enroll in; for example, Beacon Ridge Free Nights 12 still needs an AMI smart meter" ← base eligibility clause; "the off-peak energy line with the latest posting date" ← compute `LATEST(..., date_field='posted_date')`.
- Additions / omissions / meaning changes: none found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance: none (each task tool appears only in its own hub). The rebill hub's "When that line's off-peak rebill amount would exceed the care agent's adjustment limit, it is not credited here but referred to billing review as a billing dispute" is the extended rule's own sentence 2 (scope), not guidance; the dispute hub's "a correction larger than the care agent's adjustment limit is not posted as a rebill credit but referred to billing review" is the dispute rule's own replaced_by text.
- A task's opening world state written as a policy fact: none in the rendering. The computation document's "Because such a line was billed at the full contract rate" is the source baseline's own wording (see policy-side notes).

Policy-side notes (nature recorded; not a KB verdict):
- Two completed-cycle definitions coexist in the source and are both rendered: the base measure `power_msr_completed_cycles` (distinct billing period starts among energy lines whose period ended on or before the handling date; still attached to `power_signup_credit` via `measures:` although the only clause that used it was retired) in signup_and_online_credit_rules "Completed cycles. For these credits …", and the extended rule's "billing cycles that carry an on-peak or an all-hours energy charge line" in signup_credit_posting and the late-posting/usage factor documents. They agree whenever every billed cycle has ended (true here: 7 = 7) and diverge only for a cycle billed before its period ends. Source-layer redundancy, faithfully rendered.
- `power_ext_offpeak_dispute_amount` baseline assumes the largest off-peak line "was billed at the full contract rate" and computes the correct amount as billed × multiplier; on a line not billed at the full rate the formula differs from rule 1 (kWh × rate × multiplier). The KB renders the assumption verbatim. Source-layer simplification; not exercised here (the largest line is billed at the full rate).
- `power_renewal` late-election clause "at the then-valid price offer" vs `power_ext_plan_change_rate` contract-rate re-pricing (see task 0's file). Not exercised here.
- `events.power_plan_change.fields.contract_rate_cents_kwh` ("taken from the price offer valid on the plan change date") is the pre-override field meaning; schema only, not rendered, no effect.
- "billing dispute lookback" vs "billing correction lookback" wording (see task 0's file); both off-peak lines here are posted well within 12 months.
